conventions.convention: The heat operator A_h is the positive centered approximation to minus the diffusivity-weighted Laplacian. Periodic indices wrap modulo N_j; Dirichlet results use a two-dimensional rectangle.
The weighted grid inner product uses the product of spatial spacings. Dirichlet norms sum over interior nodes; boundary rows enter the stencil separately through c_h(B).
Time levels are t_n=nΔt for 0≤n≤M, with T>0, M≥1, Δt=T/M, and θ∈[0,1]. Both source and boundary contributions use endpoint weights 1−θ and θ.
The complete truncation residual includes boundary-adjacent interior rows and assumes exact sampled boundary data and continuous u_tt, u_ttt, u_xxxx and u_yyyy on the closed cylinder.
The joint Nyquist mode requires every periodic grid count N_j to be even. At the forward-Euler CFL endpoint its multiplier is −1.
The maximum-principle restriction is sufficient, not asserted necessary: Δt(1−θ)(κ_x/h_x²+κ_y/h_y²)≤1/2. The source is zero, and extrema include all initial and prescribed boundary values.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the fully discrete centered θ heat update on finite periodic rectangular grids and two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grids, including endpoint-weighted source and exact boundary contributions, and defines finite-time grid-norm power stability.

On the finite periodic rectangular d-grid, the displayed exponential modes form a basis of the complexified grid space, have eigenvalues λ_ℓ=4Σ_j κ_j h_j⁻² sin²(πℓ_j/N_j)≥0, and the zero-source θ update multiplies each mode by (1−(1−θ)Δtλ_ℓ)/(1+θΔtλ_ℓ).

On the two-dimensional rectangular zero-Dirichlet grid with positive directional diffusivities, A_h is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite in the weighted grid inner product, with the displayed horizontal and vertical edge-energy identity.

On a finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid with zero boundary data, θ∈[1/2,1] and Δt>0, one θ step with source q^n is uniquely solvable and satisfies ‖U^{n+1}‖_h≤‖U^n‖_h+2Δt‖q^n‖_h. Zero-source steps are contractive with mesh-independent constant 1.

Under the stated closed-cylinder derivative and exact-sampling hypotheses, the complete interior residual is bounded by Δt M_tt+(κ_x h_x² M_x4+κ_y h_y² M_y4)/12 for θ≠1/2, and by Δt² M_ttt/12+(κ_x h_x² M_x4+κ_y h_y² M_y4)/12 for θ=1/2.

For every finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid, Δt>0, θ∈[0,1], and interior right-hand side including known source and boundary contributions, the θ step has a unique interior solution; its implicit matrix is I+θΔt A_h.

For the zero-source finite rectangular Dirichlet θ scheme, θ∈[0,1] and Δt(1−θ)(κ_x/h_x²+κ_y/h_y²)≤1/2 imply that every interior value at every time level lies between the minimum and maximum of all initial and prescribed boundary values.

published_dependencies.used_for: Periodic-mode shift identities, products of exponential factors, and representative independence.
Exponent changes by integer multiples of 2πi leave periodic modes unchanged.
Unit modulus of imaginary exponentials and conversion of the centered stencil symbol to cosine.
Conjugate pairing of periodic modes and modulus identities in the Fourier argument.
The identity 2−2cos β=4sin²(β/2) in the heat-stencil eigenvalue calculation.
Coordinatewise orthogonality of finite periodic Fourier modes.
Factoring finite product-grid character sums and combining coordinatewise Fourier expansions.
Successive one-dimensional inversion proves spanning by the product-grid Fourier modes.

concerns.concern: The synopsis says, “For smooth solutions with matching sampled boundary rows, a complete residual estimate yields first-order time error for θ other than one half and second-order time error for Crank–Nicolson.” It omits θ∈[1/2,1], which is an explicit hypothesis of thm-parabolic-theta-scheme-global-error-bound. The definition permits θ∈[0,1], and the local residual estimate alone does not establish global convergence for the remaining values without a stability restriction. The theorem itself states the restriction correctly.

seams_checked.note: Checked the common-space interface, finite-grid lift, norm-comparison transfer lemma, and Lax theorem against the parabolic definition and estimates. The parabolic page expressly separates mesh-dependent grid-norm stability from common-space Lax equivalence; it imports no unverified lift, common-space convergence, or reverse implication.

The rectangular nodes, interior weights, zero-boundary extension, and edge differences match the elliptic definition. The Dirichlet positivity proof faithfully uses the supplier's separate directional telescoping identities, scaling them by κ_x and κ_y. No elliptic inverse or convergence estimate is imported.

Read both direct consumers: lem-periodic-advection-amplification-symbols uses only the periodic Fourier basis, while thm-periodic-centered-wave-amplification-and-endpoint also uses the one-dimensional unit-diffusivity eigenvalue 4h⁻²sin²(πℓ/N). Their periodic grid conventions agree with the supplier. Neither transfers heat time-stepping stability or a periodic conclusion to Dirichlet boundaries.
